File paths, sources & survey notes

Defaults below can be changed at installation. Code files, running processes and stored data have different lifetimes.

Path Contains
apps/saul/native/*.mts Helper and server source code
apps/saul/.build/native/ Built .mjs, JXA and board files
~/.saul/generations/g-<UUID>/ Installed code; each running process keeps its original generation
~/.saul/bridge · ~/.saul/bin Managed links and launchers for new processes
~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/ Registration files: com.saul.tabs.json and com.saul.chatgpt.json
~/.saul/run/<session>.sock Tab helper connection; new ID on reconnect
~/.saul/chatgpt/accounts.json Saul’s private account registrations and tokens
OPFS: /saul-opfs → /saul.sqlite3 Saved Saul history in Chrome’s private storage
~/Library/Application Support/Little Clarity/settings.json Shared model presets; no shared accounts or history
~/Applications/EZ.app · ~/Library/Application Support/EZ/ EZ app and local data; credentials stay in Keychain

Build → install → reconnect. Editing or rebuilding source does not replace code in an already-running helper.

ReadingRunner

Passage job manager inside offscreen
Starts
A passage request is saved, then queued.
Does
Calls the chosen provider and saves text checkpoints within 500 ms.
Stops
Completion, Stop/delete, error or offscreen loss.
Restarts
Unfinished jobs become interrupted. Only saved text survives.
Limits & sources

Two jobs per remote provider. API-compatible reading calls HTTP directly; ChatGPT uses the helper. Chrome on-device AI is disabled.

Success requires provider completion and a saved terminal record. DB_RECOVER marks queued/running/saving rows runner-lost.

reading/runner.ts · provider.ts

DigestRunner

Summary job manager inside offscreen
Starts
New summary work. A repeated selection may reuse an existing answer.
Does
Captures sources, calls ChatGPT, checks bilingual JSON and saves results.
Stops
Completion, Stop, failure or offscreen loss. Stop waits for both workers.
Restarts
Unfinished items become interrupted. Retry is explicit.
Limits, recovery & sources

One batch; two item workers. Fixed GPT-6 Luna / medium. Provider failure pauses new items; capture/format failure affects one item. Storage failure stops the batch.

Raw summary text stays in memory while streaming; it is saved at item transitions, without the reading runner’s 500 ms checkpoints. Retry uses saved sources when available; Run again captures fresh sources.

digest is the internal name for Summary, not another feature.

Database worker

SQLite-WASM in a Web Worker
Starts
Created with offscreen. SQLite opens on the first operation.
Does
Processes database requests one at a time.
Stops
Offscreen ends or the worker fails.
Remains
Committed rows survive browser restart in Chrome’s private filesystem.
Storage & sources

/saul-opfs and /saul.sqlite3 are browser-private paths, not paths at your Mac’s root. Removing the extension or clearing its data can remove history.

A worker failure rejects pending requests; there is no silent in-memory fallback.

Action helper → your module

Proposed third Node helper · not implemented
Helper
A separate local Node process, alongside the ChatGPT and tab helpers.
Module
Your trusted JS/TS file, loaded inside that process. Not another program.
Receives
Captured sources and frozen run choices; credentials stay with their owner.
Owns
Your workflow: prepare input, request generation and shape the result.
Returns
Typed result data. Saul validates, saves and renders it; no executable HTML.
Saul owns
Capture checks, account access, job state, Stop and durable history.
Draft contracts & open decisions

Proposed route: Chrome background → native messaging → action helper → your module. The other helpers keep their existing jobs; the ChatGPT helper still owns credentials.

  • Call: Summarize runs the selected handler. Loading or reloading a module does not invoke the handler.
  • Access: generation goes through a bound host interface to the existing credential owner. The interface exposes neither raw tokens nor direct database access.
  • Stop / loss: cancellation reaches the run and its helper requests. Save an honest terminal state; never resend automatically after uncertain loss.
  • Scope: one action slot and one module; existing summary is the default. Explicit Reload, no file watcher.

Still open: host start/idle/shutdown rules, result schema, code-revision retention and cancellation of child processes. Agent execution needs that last contract before it is enabled.

Trust: the interface is not a security sandbox. A Node module still has its process’s OS permissions.

Design proposal from this discussion; no installed host name, transport or source file exists yet.

Create an action, then hot-load it

Proposed journey · uses your connected ChatGPT account
  1. Ask in Saul. “Make an action that lists the claims and missing evidence.” Saul supplies the action contract to GPT.
  2. Receive a candidate. GPT returns metadata and one self-contained script in a fixed response format.
  3. Stage and check. The action helper stores a candidate revision and checks syntax and contract shape. It does not run the script yet.
  4. Choose Load or Replace. Saul shows what changes. Your click allows code loading; it does not submit a page for generation.
  5. Use the action. The next Summarize runs the new revision. Existing summary stays the default until you replace it.

Hot reload replaces the loaded revision. It does not rewrite a running function or restart Chrome, sign-in or the helper.

Load mechanics, failures & limits
  • Before Load: check the contract version, metadata, entry declaration, syntax, size and allowed imports. Store files only in a managed action directory.
  • After permission to load: start a fresh Node worker for v2. Import and verify its actual exports. Initializing a JS module executes its top-level code.
  • Switch: only after v2 is ready, update the selected revision for new runs. Keep v1 until its active runs finish. Each run records the action ID and revision.
  • Failure: syntax, import or initialization errors leave v1 selected. Discard the failed worker. This preserves selection; it cannot undo side effects from code already executed during loading.
  • No silent runs: Reload does not invoke the action handler. Failed generation is reported, not automatically sent again.
  • First version: one module, explicit Load/Replace, no watcher, npm installation or agent loop. File edits use the same stage/check/load path.

Valid is not the same as trusted. Checks can establish the format, not prove an arbitrary script’s behavior. The interface hides tokens, but Node workers still have local OS permissions; they are not a security sandbox.

Existing support: the plan helper can return generated text; no model tool-calling is needed for this journey. Generation UI, candidate storage, validation and worker replacement still need implementation.

A prompt in Saul can use its saved eligible account. A reply in chatgpt.com does not install local code by itself; it would need an import or explicit integration.

ChatGPT plan helper

Node process · com.saul.chatgpt
Starts
Chrome launches it on the first plan operation.
Does
Owns Saul login, tokens, refresh and ChatGPT HTTP/SSE calls.
Stops
Native pipe closes, a pipe fails or the process gets a stop signal. No idle timer.
Reconnects
A later request can reconnect. Failed calls are not replayed.
Connection, limits & sources

saul-chatgpt-host → plan-host.mjs. PlanService, PlanAuth and PlanStore are objects inside this process.

The background’s initPlanBridge() reuses one native port. planEvents() is a client adapter, not another process. Each operation has its own caller port.

Closing a caller cancels non-login work. Login survives popup closure. Summary’s caller is offscreen, so closing the reader does not cancel it.

Host deadline: 180 s, or 310 s for login. Bridge watchdog: 190 s / 320 s. These are limits, not observed durations.

No general shell, user-module or tab interface. Speech experiments use this same helper.

plan bridge · plan-host.mts · planEvents

Tab helper

Node process · com.saul.tabs
Starts
Chrome launches it when you enable Codex tab access.
Does
Connects local clients to Chrome through a private Unix socket.
Stops
Disable access, close the native pipe, encounter a pipe error or send a stop signal.
Reconnects
The bridge tries every minute while enabled. New connection, new session ID.
Limits & sources

saul-native-host → host.mjs. The background’s initNativeBridge() owns the port and retry alarm. Access defaults to off.

Shutdown removes the socket. Discovery ignores stale sockets left by crashes. Private directory/file modes: 0700/0600.

Browser response deadline: 30 s; client/socket deadline: 35 s. A mutation already running may finish after disconnect. Inspect tabs before retrying an uncertain change.

bridge.ts · host.mts · client.mts

saul-tabs MCP server

Node process · mcp.mts
Starts
Codex or another MCP client launches it.
Does
Exposes tab tools and serves the Tab board UI. Uses the tab helper’s socket.
Stops

Remains

Board state & sources

JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout. No self-restart supervisor. Without Chrome, discovery still works; browser operations fail.

BoardService, workspace logic and LogStore are objects in this process. Restart loses in-memory proposals and interaction tokens. Diagnostics can remain on disk.

Standalone board server

Node process · board-web.mts
Starts
You run pnpm --dir apps/saul board.
Does
Serves the Tab board on a temporary localhost port. Connects through the tab helper.
Stops
You stop the server process. Closing its browser page does not stop it.
Again
No automatic restart is configured.
Shared logic, data & sources

Uses the same BoardService and UI as MCP mode, with a local HTTP adapter. Summarize opens a Chrome reader; its source text and credentials do not go through the board.

Metadata diagnostics default to ~/.local/state/mcp-apps/saul-tab-board/<instance>. On a new service instance, recognized inactive sessions are pruned after seven days or beyond eight sessions; live owners are retained. Environment overrides can change the root.

EZ · AttemptExecution

Inside EZ.app · Swift, independent of Saul
Starts
Open EZ. Explicit Send starts one lookup Task.
Does
Saves a pending entry, authenticates, generates and saves the result.
Stops
Completion, Stop, error or quitting EZ. Hiding a view preserves work.
Restarts
Pending entries become interrupted. Requests are not sent again.
Recovery, data & sources

AppModel owns the workspace; AttemptExecution owns the job. A failed final save keeps the result in memory as Unsaved. Save again retries storage only. Unsaved bytes do not survive quitting.

History: ~/Library/Application Support/EZ/history.jsonl. Credentials: Keychain. Only model presets are shared with Saul.

EZApp.swift · AppModel.swift · AttemptExecution.swift

PDF extraction

Temporary PDF.js task inside offscreen
Starts
You choose Local PDF processing in Settings before starting the summary.
Does
Downloads bytes and extracts text with packaged PDF.js worker resources.
Stops
Success, failure, Stop or timeout. Cleanup destroys the extraction task.
Remains
Extracted source text is saved. Downloaded bytes are temporary.
Limits & sources

Local extraction: 30 s, 20 MiB, 200 pages, 120,000 characters. No OCR or chart/image understanding. Fetched PDF may differ from the open viewer.

The default attaches the PDF URL through the plan helper without downloading or parsing it in Saul. OpenAI must be able to access that URL; exact page coverage is unobserved. Retry reads the saved URL again. A provider error never switches to local extraction.
